originality.rationale: Six substantive published-finding corpus semantic queries checked Roman {2}/Italian aliases and crown, matched-bipartite, polynomial, exact-weight and minimum-function formulations. The relevant full Shao–Zhao PDF sections cover paths/trees/cycles only, excluding all crown graphs with n>=4; its cycle case covers the excluded n=3. Public full Results for the closest complete-multipartite all-weight Italian theorem and perfect Roman crown-graph theorem were read. Neither implies this ordinary Italian crown polynomial, as graph class and zero-neighbor rules differ, respectively. Earlier general algorithmic methods may compute a special instance but do not state this complete formula. Historical-priority uncertainty remains for unindexed stronger results.
residual_risks: A poorly indexed paper, thesis, or more general Roman-{2} polynomial recurrence for crown-like graphs might imply the formula.

value.rationale: The complete labeled-function weight distribution on dense regular crown graphs is a natural extension of the newly studied Italian polynomial, not merely the scalar domination number. The deleted matching induces a matched-index constraint absent from complete multipartite examples; the full polynomial and exceptional n=4 minimum count expose nontrivial structure needed for future counting/probabilistic applications. The claim is not a renaming of perfect Roman or usual domination.
